title: layer-aware-kv-reshaper-and-batch-smoothing-for-ultra-long-seq-variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: For ultra-long-context workloads (8k-1M tokens) we observe pathological KV residency hotspots in specific attention layers for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants. These hotspots increase GPU fragmentation, force high eviction churn, and cause tail latency spikes when continuous batching coalesces heterogeneous sequence lengths.

Goal: Implement a layer-aware KV residency reshaper + batch-smoothing policy that reduces per-layer residency variance, lowers eviction churn, and preserves SLOs while keeping token-cost efficiency. Target models: Llama-2-13B/70B (long variants), Mistral long-window variants, Qwen-Extended. This ticket designs the memory profile, lands the runtime changes, and coordinates experiments and rollout.

High-level approach:
- Telemetry: add per-layer residency histograms (age, bytes, live-requests) during runtime sampling windows.
- Reshaper: introduce soft per-layer residency caps and proportional shrink/grow actions executed at batch boundaries. The reshaper uses a token-age-decay score to prioritize older KV entries for eviction within a layer and migrates hot entries to a short-term slab to reduce scatter.
- Batch smoother: modify continuous-batching selector to prefer grouping requests with similar cumulative KV footprints and token-age distributions (token-age histogram fingerprint). When not possible, the smoother emits a conservative packing hint to the allocator to reserve temporary prefetch budget.
- Allocator changes: support temporary short-lived slab pools for "hotset" items, per-layer bucket quotas, and a fast fallback path that compresses stored KV to 8-bit quantized representations when memory pressure is high for specific layers.
- Compatibility: behavior configurable via runtime flags and model-profile metadata (model-family + long-context flag).

Why different from previous memory-profile work: prior tickets tuned global footprints and coarse KV segmentation. This work moves to layer-granular policies and integrates continuous-batching signals (token-age and pack-fingerprint) into residency decisions to avoid cross-request interference in hot layers.
acceptance_criteria: Per-layer residency variance reduced by >=30% vs baseline on Llama-2-70B long variant under representative mix of 4k-256k seqlen workload (measured by 99th/median ratio)
Eviction churn (bytes evicted per minute) reduced by >=25% on Qwen-Extended during steady state high concurrency runs
Tail latency (p95/p99 generation token latency) not worsened by >10% for P99 latency SLOs compared to baseline and ideally improves p95 by at least 5%
Memory fragmentation (external fragmentation measure from allocator telemetry) improves or remains within 5% of baseline under mixed model fleet runs
Feature is gated behind a runtime config and per-model profile; rollout can be toggled and auto-rolled back by canary if regressed quality or latency observed
comments: 2026-02-22 Aisha Patel: Initial design doc drafted. Decided to pursue layer-aware quotas instead of per-parameter tracking to keep allocator overhead low.

2026-02-28 Mateo Chen: Prototype telemetry landed in dev runtime (build rt-1.20.8). Added per-layer histogram wires; sampling window 500ms. Observed L2 attention layer 18 accounting for 42% of hot entries in a 32k-window test.

2026-03-03 Performance: ran mixed seqlen 4k/16k/64k stress tests on a 8xA100 cluster. Baseline eviction churn 1.9GB/min; early reshaper prototype reduced to 1.3GB/min but increased p95 token latency by 7% for the 64k tail case.

2026-03-05 Design decision: introduce 'hot-slab' short-term pool and token-age eviction ranking to avoid global evictions. Also decided to quantize low-access KV to 8-bit as a mid-flight fallback; quantization chosen to keep reconstruction cost < 150us.
2026-03-07 Eng review: PR #4281 opened for allocator changes (short-slab + per-layer quotas). Requesting review from @sophia.nguyen and @benjamin-roberts on allocator correctness and metrics hooks.

2026-03-09 Experiment: enabled batch-smoother fingerprinting. Mixed workload p95 improved 6% relative to prototype; p99 stable. Observed slight increase in bin-packing overhead (3% extra CPU), acceptable.

2026-03-10 Mateo Chen: Merged PRs to staging; plan canary rollout to 10% of production Dedicated clusters next week. Monitoring dashboards prepared: residency-variance, eviction-churn, slab-usage, latency-by-seqlen.
Open: need QA for quantized-KV reconstruction edge cases (rare numeric drift) and to add model-profile metadata for Qwen-Extended (PM follow-up).
